cover.headline: The market prices JLR near the bottom of its own post-demerger range: cheap, if the new Range Rovers deliver
cover.lead: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles is Jaguar Land Rover (81% of revenue) plus India's #2 car maker, after trucks were demerged in Oct-2025. JLR lost FY26 to tariffs, China and a cyber attack (EBIT 0.7%) and made only 2.8% in Q1FY27; India grew volumes 46% but earned a 4.3% EBITDA margin. We forecast EPS of ₹21.4 / ₹38.6 / ₹44.0 for FY27-29E, assuming JLR misses its c.4% FY27 guidance but recovers to ~11-12% EBITDA margins as four new models and GBP1.7bn of savings arrive. The street values the stock on a **sum of the parts**; on the house rule we apply **JLR 2x and India PV 12x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA** plus Tata Technologies at market, less net debt and minority claims: **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). We initiate with BUY.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}: a wide range, because JLR's margin is the whole case.

arguments.h: India: share gains are real, profits are not yet
arguments.p: Wholesales +46% in Q1FY27 (industry +24%), Vahan share 14.3%, ~40% of India's EV market and bookings ~3.5x pre-crisis. But commodities took 4.5% of revenue and price rises only 1%: EBITDA 4.3% incl. PLI. We model ₹74,367 cr of revenue in FY27E at 5.8%, rising to 7.0% in FY28E before PLI ends.

arguments.h: JLR: FY27 is a bridge year; FY28 is the test
arguments.p: FY27 guidance (GBP26bn, c.4% EBIT, FCF breakeven) needs ~4.4% for the rest of the year after Q1's 2.8%; we assume ~3.5%. FY28 brings Range Rover Electric and Sport Electric, Range Rover GT and Jaguar Type 01, ASP "well north of GBP80,000" and the cost programme: we model 11.0% EBITDA, in line with Emkay's 5.7% EBIT.

arguments.h: Debt is manageable, but it is JLR's
arguments.p: Net debt ₹42.2K cr at Jun-2026 (JLR GBP3.6bn; India net cash ₹8K cr) after a GBP2.2bn FY26 outflow; liquidity GBP5.9bn. JLR invests GBP3.7bn a year, so EBITDA overstates cash: one reason the market pays only 1-3x for it.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price implies ~1.4x for JLR
arguments.p: Valuing India PV like Maruti (13.1x forward EV/EBITDA since 2021) and Tata Technologies at market, TMPV's price implied a median 2.1x EBITDA for JLR since the demerger and 1.4x on 30-Sep-2026. De-rated, 2x on Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹41,103 cr gives our target; at the market's current 1.4x it would be ₹305.

sections.title: The demerger, the cyber attack and new leaders: a company reset in twelve months

blocks.p: Tata Motors was India's biggest truck maker that also owned JLR and a small car business. Over 2021-2025 it split itself up: private investors bought convertible preference shares in the EV unit (TPEML), Tata Technologies listed (Nov-2023), the vehicle-finance arm merged into Tata Capital (May-2025) and, effective 1-Oct-2025, the commercial-vehicle business was demerged into a separately listed company (TMCV, listed 12-Nov-2025) with one TMCV share for each Tata Motors share. The listed parent kept the cars and JLR and was renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. Weeks earlier, a cyber attack had shut every JLR plant for September 2025.

sections.title: Two markets moving in opposite directions: Indian cars booming, global luxury cars squeezed

blocks.p: **India.** Car sales reached a record 47.0 lakh in FY26 (+8%), with H2 up 17% after the GST cut of Sep-2025; Q1FY27 grew 24% to ~13 lakh on a low base. Greener fuels are taking over: EVs and CNG were 31% of Q1FY27 sales and EVs alone 8% in June 2026 (2 lakh+ EVs sold in FY26). Management expects the market to grow 6-7% a year to ~64 lakh by FY31, with nearly half the growth from EVs. The catch is costs: commodities (aluminium, copper, precious metals) rose sharply after the Middle East conflict, costing Tata 4.5% of revenue in Q1FY27 with ~3% more in Q2.

**Global luxury cars.** JLR: China luxury tax from mid-Jul-2025 and weak demand (China wholesales -27% in FY26, -25% in Q1FY27); US tariffs on UK cars 27.5% until the UK-US deal cut them to 10% within a quota (incremental tariff cost ~GBP525m in FY26); Middle East (6% of sales) hit by the Iran conflict in Q1FY27; VME (discounts) 7.1% of revenue in Q1FY27 vs 4.1%. JLR says the industry's challenges (geopolitics, inflation, supply chains, regulation) are intensifying, and Chinese brands are winning their home market.

bullets: **Tariffs.** US duty on UK-built cars fell from 27.5% to 10% (within a quota) under the UK-US deal; JLR's incremental tariff cost was ~GBP525m in FY26, half offset by lower US emissions costs. JLR is exploring US production with Stellantis (MoU; definitive agreement targeted by end-2026).

**Electrification.** Europe and the UK push EV mandates (Euro 7 from 2027); JLR launches four BEVs over FY27-28 and expects them to be margin-neutral. In India, the PLI scheme pays incentives on EVs and advanced cars until FY28.

**Currency.** JLR prefers a weak pound: its US dollar sales are hedged (book around 1.28 USD/GBP); the pound averaged 1.32 in Q1FY27. In rupees, a weaker rupee (₹128 per pound in Q1FY27 vs ₹119 in FY26) lifts reported revenue.

sections.title: Peak investment: ₹42K cr of capex a year for new JLR platforms and India capacity

blocks.p: This is a capital-hungry business. JLR spent GBP3.6bn in FY26 (GBP2.6bn of it on engineering, 64% capitalised) and guides GBP3.7bn for FY27, as it launches three new architectures (the electric Range Rovers, the EMA platform for Range Rover GT, and Jaguar's Type 01); the five-year plan is GBP18bn from FY24. India invested ₹5,218 cr in FY26 (capex ₹4,300 cr, 7.5% of revenue, plus expensed R&D) and plans ~7% a year to FY31 with a front-loaded step-up for capacity (0.9 mn to 1.3 mn units). We model consolidated capex of ₹42,000 / ₹41,500 / ₹41,000 cr in FY27-29E against depreciation of ₹20-26K cr. Returns are low: ROCE was 3% in FY26 on Screener's basis, and we forecast ROE of only {{fin.roe.12|pct}} / {{fin.roe.13|pct}} / {{fin.roe.14|pct}} in FY27-29E.

Shareholders get ~₹3-8 a share of dividends. Value creation depends on the new JLR models earning their cost of capital; on our numbers JLR's return on capital stays below 10% until FY29.

sections.title: Earnings quality: complex, with one-offs every year and a big accounting gain in FY26

bullets: **FY26 profit is an accounting artefact.** ₹82,390 cr of attributable profit includes an ₹82,616 cr non-cash gain on distributing the CV business to shareholders (no effect on net worth); the continuing business lost ₹1,632 cr. The annual report's EPS is −₹0.61; Screener's ₹223.74 includes the gain.

**Exceptional items recur.** FY26: ₹4,142 cr (cyber ₹2,786 cr, employee separation ₹1,044 cr, demerger costs ₹422 cr); JLR also ran a voluntary redundancy programme (~500 managers and staff, Q2FY26). We do not forecast exceptional items, so our EPS is "before exceptionals".
**Grants are a large share of EBITDA.** ₹3,603 cr of grant income in FY26 (16% of company EBITDA), of which India PLI ₹1,044 cr; PLI ends after FY28.

**Capitalised engineering.** JLR capitalised 64% of engineering spend in FY26 and 74% in Q1FY27 (₹76,154 cr of intangibles under development at Mar-26). Higher capitalisation flatters EBITDA; amortisation follows when the cars launch.
**Currency and hedges.** JLR's EBITDA includes realised hedges; unrealised FX and commodity revaluations swing PBT by GBP100m+ a quarter.
**Deferred tax.** A ₹14,976 cr deferred tax asset (Mar-26) on UK losses produced a tax credit in FY26; future tax will run near 30% once JLR is profitable.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Clean audit (B S R & Co.), transparent segment disclosure and reconciliations, but reported profit is hard to use: demerger gain, recurring exceptionals, grant-dependent India margins and high engineering capitalisation.

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's #2 and fastest-growing car maker with ~40% of its electric-car market, and Jaguar Land Rover, a luxury SUV maker with three of the strongest nameplates in the industry, four new models coming and a GBP1.7bn cost programme. Plus 53% of Tata Technologies.

**What you are paying:** ₹283.5, 7.3x our FY28E EPS and 6.9x Sep-28E. After valuing India PV like Maruti (de-rated) and Tata Technologies at market, the price implies ~1.4x EBITDA for JLR, below the 2.1x the stock itself implied on average since the demerger. Our target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}) assumes JLR earns ~11-12% EBITDA margins again in FY28-29E; management has guided only FY27.

segments._why: Revenue = GBP revenue x INR/GBP (jlrBuild). EBITDA margin (Ind AS segment): 14.3% FY25, 6.7% FY26 (cyber), 8.1% Q1FY27 (EBIT 2.8%). Guidance c.4% EBIT for FY27; we assume 3.5% (Q1 2.8%, China 'may get worse before it stabilises', VME 7.1%), i.e. ~8.8% EBITDA with D&A ~5.3% of revenue. FY28E 11.0% (EBIT ~5.7%): four launches (Range Rover Electric and Sport Electric, Range Rover GT, Jaguar Type 01) and the GBP1.7bn cost programme; FY29E 11.8%. Street: Emkay EBIT 4.0%/5.7% FY27/28E.

FY27E 5.8% (H2 step-up from PLI on new models, price rises, cost cuts), FY28E 7.0%, FY29E 6.0% because PLI (~2.3% of revenue) ends after FY28 and cost cuts only partly replace it.
